name: Stochastic Patchwork
miniText: How is the variability of a sample proportion related to the number of independent trials? NetLogo Stochastic Patchwork repeatedly recolors a selected block of patches using the same target probability, then accumulates the fraction in the target color. Durrett [1] grounds the resulting Bernoulli sum and its mean, Berry [2] frames finite-sample Gaussian approximation, and Wilensky [3] connects constructive simulation with understanding distributional regularity. Larger blocks average more local random decisions, while changing the target probability changes both the mean and variability. Spatial adjacency is visual organization: the baseline color draws do not copy neighboring colors. Repeated histograms therefore illustrate sampling distributions rather than spatial contagion. Finite samples, discrete proportions, and probabilities close to zero or one limit bell-curve intuition. The experiment provides no evidence that a real spatial population has independent observations.
